title: May 2024 iOS privacy manifest requirements tracking issue
body:
### **UPDATE**
[We now have guide on how to add a privacy manifest via your app config (app.json / app.config.js)](https://docs.expo.dev/guides/apple-privacy/).

---

### Overview

Recently, [Apple announced](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=3d8a9yyh) that, starting May 1, they would start enforcing that all new apps and updates must declare approved reasons for using specific APIs in a privacy manifest, preventing uploads to TestFlight if the requirement is not met. These requirements also apply to 3rd party SDK's, with specific SDK's identified by Apple [requiring a signature](https://developer.apple.com/support/third-party-SDK-requirements/) in addition to the manifest. 

If you submitted to TestFlight after March 13th, you may have received an email from Apple with an "ITMS-91053" warning, indicating that they found API usage matching an `NSPrivacyAccessedAPI` category in your app that will require these changes in order to meet the requirements after May 1st (common categories might include `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace` and `NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp`).

### What Expo is doing about it

Expo engineers are actively engaged with this issue, doing everything in our power ensure that your app submissions continue uninterrupted despite the relatively short notice:
- Adding privacy manifests to all affected modules maintained by Expo
- Tracking progress on key dependencies not maintained by Expo (e.g., this [PR to add the manifest to `react-native`](https://github.com/facebook/react-native/pull/42979)) and ensuring our version validation is updated accordingly as these updates go live.
- Providing guidance on how to add the privacy manifest to community-maintained modules
- Providing guidance and/or tooling to add the privacy info to your CNG-compatible app as needed

As this potentially requires action by any number of 3rd party library maintainers, we can't guarantee that you will not see a rejection for this reason from Apple after May 1st. However, we are focused on taking care of what is in our control, and providing guidance on what is outside of our control.

### What's next

We expect to have more specific information about the steps we're taking to address this requirement, including more information about action required on your end to keep your iOS app submissions running smoothly past May 1st.

We will keep this issue open and will post updates here, so watch this issue to keep up-to-date!

The current warning is just that- a warning. You can still build and submit and publish to the stores without any changes before May 1st, and app versions already available in the store will have the same functionality they always had (so, if you built it with updates, it will still have updates). I'm not aware of a previous cutoff like this where builds were retroactively invalidated.

comments.body:
Thought I'd give a bit of an update related to privacy manifests.

As many of you know, by May 1st a privacy file will be required to be included with your project for a fairly large set of APIs.
Here's what we're currently doing to ensure this will not cause any interruptions to the development and release experience for Expo users:

# Defining your own privacy reason APIs

We have a new default config plugin merged to core in https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/28005. This plugins runs on every prebuild or `run` action, as long as you define the `expo.ios.privacyManifests` dictionary in `app.json`. Full docs and a release are coming out once ready.

The plugin creates or expands a `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` file included in the iOS project, and I've successfully tested that reasons added there result in the API not being mentioned in any warning emails from AppStoreConnect, so I'm fairly optimistic this will work beyond the May 1st deadline.

# Using expo or other 3rd party packages.

All expo packages are included in the iOS project using cocoapods, and the wider community has aligned on a specific standard of defining xcprivacy files as `resource_bundles` in those pods.

At the same time, we're seeing no success in apple review process picking up those files from such dependencies, so we're not sure if this will actually work beyond May 1st. (https://github.com/participant112community/discussions-and-proposals/discussions/776#discussioncomment-8961835)

We're in a fairly good place with several options for either doing that automatically as a build step ( a PR is in review in https://github.com/expo/expo/pull/28091), providing a list for our users to copy into the app.json properties to be handled by the default config plugin, but for now you can expect to receive warning emails when using some of Expo SDK packages.

I'm fully expecting a fix for this to be ready well before May 1st, with more details and docs coming ASAP.

I originally received Apple warning emails about:

```
NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryDiskSpace
NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryFileTimestamp
```

**My first steps to resolve this:**
1. Add these two privacy types (and necessary reasons) to my `app.config.json`
2. Kicked off a TestFlight build
3. Added an "External Group" to this build
4. Waited to see if the warning Apple email would arrive

**After performing the above, I then got an email from Apple stating that these were "missing API declaration"** 

```
NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategorySystemBootTime
NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults
```

I was pretty confused as to how these two missing privacy types are **now** being flagged, but weren't originally. 

When I run the prebuild locally using `npx expo prebuild --clean -p ios` without any configuration in my `app.config.json`, no `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` file was being generated, so I **assumed that I never had one** at root level.

What's interesting is that after inspecting the IPA built by EAS _(steps below)_, I **did** have a root level `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` file! I then _manually_ combined these together in my `app.config.json`, which **prevented the warning emails from Apple**.

**Steps to inspect your build (works on Mac, not tested on Windows):**
1. Download the generated IPA file from EAS (a build **prior** to adding any custom manifest to your `app.config.json)
2. Rename the downloaded file extension from `.ipa` to `.zip`
3. Extract the contents
5. Go to the "Payload" folder and right click your application. Select "Show Package Contents"
6. See if a `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` file is generated at the root of this
7. If there is, you will need to copy this configuration in `PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy` to your `app.config.json` (if you are manually specifying it)

It seems like we need to be careful when specifying a manifest manually injected via `app.config.json`. **This could overwrite the root one** (if it was generated by 3rd party libraries, although I'm not sure how that currently works). There might be an easier way to ensure the privacy manifests are combined, but doing it manually seemed to work for me.

For anyone having issues with `“Multiple commands produce …PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy”` errors (@participant74):

This could be caused by `participant112branch`. The latest version of this package uses the underlying iOS Branch SDK 3.2.0, which incorrectly links their privacy manifest file. This issue was fixed on version 3.4.1 of the SDK ([see changelog](https://github.com/BranchMetrics/ios-branch-deep-linking-attribution/releases/tag/3.4.1)).

Unfortunately, Sentry doesn't have an issue log in their official repo (seriously, Branch? Be better), so no one can figure this out based on other people's findings.

The solution for now is to use a patch with `patch-package` and pin the iOS SDK to 3.4.1:
- Go to `./node_modules/participant112branch/participant112branch.podspec`
- Change `s.dependency 'BranchSDK', '3.2.0'` into `s.dependency 'BranchSDK', '3.4.1'`
- Open your terminal and run `npx patch-package`
- Commit the generated patch into git and this should fix your builds.

I've been working to update an SDK project to support this, and came across a few issues primarily related to versioning issues. I was experiencing issues regarding `withPrivacyInfo` being undefined even though I'd installed the appropriate versions.

For anyone having issues on SDK50 and has already followed info in this thread, here's a few additional things to check:

 - `yarn why @expo/config-plugins` - this will show which versions of the config plugins library are being used. As of writing, it should be `7.9.1` for all items listed.

 - `yarn why expo` - this will show which version of expo is being used. As of writing, this should be `50.0.17` but if you're using the pre-SDK50 fixes listed earlier in this thread, this may differ
 
 - If you're working in a monorepo, make sure that the versions match between packages/folders within the workspace
 
 - You can make use of `resolutions` in your `package.json` file to pin the specific versions if you're having issues with earlier versions being referenced in the commands above
 
 - If you're using an `app.config.js` file (as opposed to `app.json`) and have custom logic to determine what config should be output (e.g. you're passing in variables as part of a build command), make sure that you're always returning the `privacyManifests` field on all possible outputs. For example, if you have a JS object called `devConfig`, another called `stagingConfig`, and another called `prodConfig` (where all 3 are valid appconfigs), make sure your `privacyManifests` is in all of them.

For me, the issue was that I'd got `@expo/config-plugins` set as `7.8.0` (project-specific reasons) and it was causing issues even after updating. Your project might not need these resolutions at all, so consider removing them if you're confident you don't need them.
